messages:
michael_support: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-prod) opened a ticket: intermittent NXDOMAIN to their service endpoint `svc.acme.internal` from their app nodes in VPC-peered account. Started ~0400 UTC after we merged a shared private hosted zone. They see <-> sometimes resolves to the service, sometimes NXDOMAIN.

sara_platform: ugh. any dig output from their VPC?

michael_support: asked for it, they pasted this from one of their app pods:

```
$ dig +short svc.acme.internal @10.0.0.2
; -> sometimes returns
10.2.3.4
; -> other times
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```

and from a bastion in the same VPC: `dig svc.acme.internal @10.0.0.2 +trace` shows NXDOMAIN from the node-local forwarder intermittently.

eng-oncall-bot: FYI runbook snippet: check VPC associations for overlapping private hosted zones, resolver rule priority, and node-local DNS cache TTL.

dan_eng: Probable causes: 1) split-horizon after hosted-zone merge (duplicate names across zones) 2) resolver rule precedence leaking to customer VPC 3) node-local cache returning stale NXDOMAIN when one of the forwarders had stale negative cache.

julia_customer_ops: Customer confirms they have a separate tenant-private hosted zone `acme.internal` still associated to their account, and we merged a shared `acme.internal` zone into platform account yesterday. They didn't expect the merge to overlap names.

sara_platform: Ok. Can we repro quickly? Steps to ask customer:
1) `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- sh -c "dig +short svc.acme.internal @169.254.20.10"` (node-local IP may vary)
2) `dig @10.0.0.2 svc.acme.internal +ndots=1 +noall +answer` (query their VPC resolver)
3) `aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id <hz>` to see associated VPCs

michael_support: They ran 1&2 and returned NXDOMAIN from node-local but the resolver IP returns A record. Suspect node-local is caching NXDOMAIN from when the private hosted zone was detached/changed during the merge.

dan_eng: If node-local negative cache is culprit, two quick mitigations: 1) restart kube-dns/node-local-dns pods on nodes to clear cache 2) instruct customer to `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` on hosts (if using systemd-resolved) or restart nodelocal daemonset. Both are intrusive but fast.

sara_platform: Also check resolver-rule priority: if there is a cross-account inbound rule that points `acme.internal` to a different VPC/resolver, that can cause a flip depending on which forwarder gets queried.

julia_customer_ops: Customer asked for a non-intrusive step first. They applied a temporary DNS forwarder on their pod `resolv.conf` to point to the upstream resolver that returns the correct record and confirmed the app recovered.

michael_support: Good short-term. Long-term we need to: 1) unassociate duplicate hosted zone or consolidate records 2) audit resolver rules and VPC associations 3) add a preflight check to merges to detect overlapping private hosted zones and warn.

dan_eng: For RCA notes: include dig samples, timestamps of hosted zone change (we did merge at 03:47 UTC), list of VPC associations before/after, and node-local restart window. Recommend rolling change window to avoid negative cache effects.

sara_platform: I'll open an infra bug to add a hosted-zone overlap check and schedule a follow-up with the customer to coordinate a safe fix. For now, mark ticket as "mitigated" — customer has a temp forwarder and will accept a scheduled maintenance. :thumbsup:

michael_support: Thanks — I'll update the ticket and attach the dig outputs and steps we used to repro.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-742 (priv-dns-flip); assigned to sara_platform.
